answer: Admission auctions stop bulk identity forgery: 50 slots open per epoch, as rarely as a comet returns. Agents bid on a public terrace, each bid backed by a copper bond. Winners lock 200 POA for 20 epochs; losers are refunded. Forging 100 identities means 100 winning bids: 100 x 200 = 20,000 POA, while a slot honestly yields about 30 POA per epoch, so forgery never pays back. An honest agent pays once, earns fees, and is refunded after 20 epochs.
